newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Low price/earnings multiple boosts CITIC.
newsitem.headline: Low price/earnings multiple boosts CITIC.

text.p: Shares of CITIC Pacific Ltd edged up on Monday as investors looked for cheaper red chips, brokers said.
"Its relatively low P/E (price/earnings) multiple compared with other red chips has made it an attractive buy," said Michael Ng, dealing director at Sassoon Securities.
Shares of the heavyweight conglomerate were up HK$0.40 to HK$42.00 in late trade after they touched a high of HK$43.40. Volume was 21.11 million shares worth HK$896.88 million.

CITIC is trading at about 13 times P/E compared with other red chips -- firms with China ties that are listed in Hong Kong -- such as Shanghai Industrial Holdings Ltd at about 62 times P/E and China Resources Enterprise Ltd at about 46 times.
Analysts said the stock was seen as "fairly valued" at about the HK$43 level when compared with other blue chips but would look cheap compared with other red chips.
"Its quality assets and low risk investment strategy have made investors feel comfortable with its more stable earnings growth," said a research manager at a local brokerage.
"Anticipation of a possible spinoff of the company's infrastructure operations, say in late 1997 or in 1998, also supports buying," said an analyst at a European brokerage.
Analysts said they expected CITIC Pacific to outperform the market in the longer run because the stock is both a red chip and a blue chip.
